titulo: This Is Me: School Life and Daily Routines
titulo_es: Este soy yo: vida escolar y rutinas diarias
estandares: Comprendo información personal que dan mis compañeros y mi profesor. Identifico elementos culturales como nombres propios y lugares en textos sencillos. Leo y entiendo textos auténticos sencillos sobre hechos concretos asociados a tradiciones culturales que conozco.
competencias: Leer y escribir textos cortos con Wh- questions y demostrativos; crear oraciones y diálogos simples con saludos y rutinas en presente simple; hablar y escuchar para pedir y dar información específica sobre personas, lugares y actividades.
componentes: Pensamiento crítico, comunicación, colaboración y creatividad.

proyecto.descripcion_es: Cada estudiante arma un lap book (cuadernillo desplegable) con secciones: mi información personal, mi apariencia, mi rutina diaria en presente simple, mis amigos y datos curiosos sobre mí.
proyecto.descripcion_en: Each student builds a lap book with sections: my personal information, my appearance, my daily routine in simple present, my friends and fun facts about me.

lecciones.content_es:
El verbo más usado del inglés

To be significa ser y estar. Cambia según la persona: I am, you are, he/she/it is, we/you/they are.

Las tres formas

  • Afirmativa: I am a student. (I'm)
  • Negativa: She is not tired. (isn't)
  • Interrogativa: Are you ready? — se invierte el orden.

Cuidado

En español decimos «tengo 12 años», pero en inglés se usa to be: I am 12 years old, nunca I have 12 years.
lecciones.content_en:
The most used verb in English

To be works as both ser and estar in Spanish. It changes with the person: I am, you are, he/she/it is, we/you/they are.

The three forms

  • Affirmative: I am a student. (I'm)
  • Negative: She is not tired. (isn't)
  • Question: Are you ready? — the order is inverted.

Watch out

Age uses to be, not have: I am 12 years old, never I have 12 years.

fichas.d: Yo soy / yo estoy. Contracción: I'm.
fichas.d_en: First person singular of to be. Contraction: I'm.

fichas.d: Tercera persona singular: is. Contracción: he's, she's, it's.
fichas.d_en: Third person singular: is. Contraction: he's, she's, it's.

fichas.d: Negaciones contraídas de is not y are not.
fichas.d_en: Contracted negatives of is not and are not.

fichas.d: Pregunta con to be: el verbo va antes del sujeto.
fichas.d_en: Question with to be: the verb goes before the subject.

fichas.d: La edad se dice con to be, no con have.
fichas.d_en: Age is expressed with to be, not with have.

quiz.why: My sister es tercera persona singular, así que usa is.
quiz.why_en: My sister is third person singular, so it takes is.

quiz.q: ¿Cuál es la forma negativa correcta de «They are late»?
quiz.q_en: Which is the correct negative form of "They are late"?
quiz.why: Con to be la negación se hace agregando not al verbo: are not / aren't.
quiz.why_en: With to be you negate by adding not to the verb: are not / aren't.

quiz.q_en: How do you ask "Are you Colombian?"
quiz.why: En preguntas con to be el verbo se pone antes del sujeto: Are you…?
quiz.why_en: In to be questions the verb goes before the subject: Are you…?

lecciones.content_es:
¿Para qué sirven?

Reemplazan al sujeto para no repetir el nombre: Ana is my friend. She is funny.

Los siete

  • I – yo (siempre en mayúscula)
  • you – tú / usted / ustedes
  • he – él · she – ella · it – ello (cosas y animales)
  • we – nosotros · they – ellos/ellas

Regla de oro

En inglés el sujeto nunca se omite. No se dice Is my friend, se dice He is my friend.
lecciones.content_en:
What are they for?

They replace the subject so you don't repeat the name: Ana is my friend. She is funny.

The seven

  • I – always capitalized
  • you – singular and plural
  • he · she · it (things and animals)
  • we · they

Golden rule

English never drops the subject. Not Is my friend, but He is my friend.

fichas.d: Yo. Se escribe siempre con mayúscula, vaya donde vaya.
fichas.d_en: First person singular. Always written with a capital letter.

fichas.d: Se usa para cosas, animales y el clima: It is cold.
fichas.d_en: Used for things, animals and the weather: It is cold.

fichas.d: Ellos o ellas, para personas y también para cosas en plural.
fichas.d_en: Used for people and also for plural things.

fichas.d: El inglés siempre necesita sujeto explícito en la oración.
fichas.d_en: English always needs an explicit subject in the sentence.

quiz.q: «Carlos and I go to school.» ¿Qué pronombre reemplaza a «Carlos and I»?
quiz.q_en: "Carlos and I go to school." Which pronoun replaces "Carlos and I"?
quiz.why: Cuando el hablante se incluye en el grupo, el pronombre es we.
quiz.why_en: When the speaker is part of the group, the pronoun is we.

quiz.q_en: Which pronoun do we use for "the dog"?
quiz.why: Los animales y las cosas en singular toman it.
quiz.why_en: Singular animals and things take it.

quiz.why: El sujeto va primero y no se puede omitir: She is my teacher.
quiz.why_en: The subject comes first and cannot be dropped: She is my teacher.

lecciones.content_es:
De quién es

Van antes del sustantivo y dicen a quién pertenece: my book, her bag.

La pareja de cada pronombre

  • I → my · you → your · he → his
  • she → her · it → its
  • we → our · they → their

El error clásico

its (su, de ello) no lleva apóstrofe. it's con apóstrofe significa it is.

Además, el posesivo no cambia si el objeto es plural: my books, no mys books.
lecciones.content_en:
Showing who owns something

They go before the noun and tell who it belongs to: my book, her bag.

The pair for each pronoun

  • I → my · you → your · he → his
  • she → her · it → its
  • we → our · they → their

The classic mistake

its has no apostrophe. it's with an apostrophe means it is.

Possessives never take -s: my books, not mys books.

fichas.d: Mi y tu(s). Van antes del sustantivo: my pencil.
fichas.d_en: They go before the noun: my pencil, your pencil.

fichas.d: his = de él; her = de ella. Depende del dueño, no del objeto.
fichas.d_en: his = of him; her = of her. It depends on the owner, not the object.

fichas.d: its = su (de ello). it's = it is.
fichas.d_en: its = possessive. it's = it is.

fichas.d: Nuestro y de ellos: our school, their books.
fichas.d_en: our school, their books.

quiz.why: El dueño es Sofía, mujer, así que el posesivo es her.
quiz.why_en: The owner is Sofía, so the possessive is her.

quiz.why: Our es el adjetivo posesivo que acompaña al sustantivo classroom.
quiz.why_en: Our is the possessive adjective that goes with the noun classroom.

quiz.why: Para un animal usamos its, sin apóstrofe.
quiz.why_en: For an animal we use its, with no apostrophe.

lecciones.content_es:
¿Cuándo se usa?

Para hábitos, rutinas y verdades generales: I study English every day.

La -s de la tercera persona

Con he, she, it el verbo lleva -s: She plays soccer.

  • Verbos en -ch, -sh, -ss, -x, -o → -es: watch → watches, go → goes
  • Consonante + y → -ies: study → studies
  • have → has (irregular)

Palabras que lo acompañan

every day, always, usually, on Mondays, in the morning.
lecciones.content_en:
When do we use it?

For habits, routines and general truths: I study English every day.

The third person -s

With he, she, it the verb takes -s: She plays soccer.

  • Verbs ending in -ch, -sh, -ss, -x, -o → -es: watch → watches, go → goes
  • Consonant + y → -ies: study → studies
  • have → has (irregular)

Signal words

every day, always, usually, on Mondays, in the morning.

fichas.d: Solo la tercera persona singular lleva -s en presente simple.
fichas.d_en: Only third person singular takes -s in the simple present.

fichas.d: Consonante + y se convierte en -ies.
fichas.d_en: Consonant + y becomes -ies.

fichas.d: Verbos en -o, -ch, -sh, -ss, -x agregan -es.
fichas.d_en: Verbs ending in -o, -ch, -sh, -ss, -x add -es.

fichas.d: Único verbo totalmente irregular en la tercera persona.
fichas.d_en: The only fully irregular verb in the third person.

fichas.d: Expresión típica del presente simple: todos los días.
fichas.d_en: Typical simple present time expression.

quiz.why: Watch termina en -ch, así que en tercera persona agrega -es.
quiz.why_en: Watch ends in -ch, so the third person adds -es.

quiz.why: They es plural: el verbo va sin -s.
quiz.why_en: They is plural: the verb takes no -s.

quiz.q_en: What is the third person of "study"?
quiz.why: Consonante + y → se cambia la y por -ies.
quiz.why_en: Consonant + y → change the y to -ies.

lecciones.content_es:
El ayudante do / does

Para negar y preguntar en presente simple usamos do (I, you, we, they) y does (he, she, it).

Negación

  • I don't like fish.
  • He doesn't like fish.

Pregunta

  • Do you play chess? → Yes, I do. / No, I don't.
  • Does she play chess? → Yes, she does. / No, she doesn't.

Clave

Cuando aparece does, el verbo principal pierde la -s: Does he play?, no Does he plays?
lecciones.content_en:
The helper do / does

To make negatives and questions in the simple present we use do (I, you, we, they) and does (he, she, it).

Negative

  • I don't like fish.
  • He doesn't like fish.

Question

  • Do you play chess? → Yes, I do. / No, I don't.
  • Does she play chess? → Yes, she does. / No, she doesn't.

Key point

When does appears, the main verb loses the -s: Does he play?, not Does he plays?

fichas.d: Negación del presente simple: do not y does not.
fichas.d_en: Simple present negatives: do not and does not.

fichas.d: Con does el verbo principal va sin -s.
fichas.d_en: With does the main verb takes no -s.

fichas.d: Yes, I do. / No, she doesn't. Nunca se repite el verbo principal.
fichas.d_en: Yes, I do. / No, she doesn't. The main verb is never repeated.

fichas.d: Do/Does + sujeto + verbo base + complemento.
fichas.d_en: Do/Does + subject + base verb + complement.

quiz.why: Your sister es he/she/it, así que la pregunta empieza con Does.
quiz.why_en: Your sister is third person singular, so the question starts with Does.

quiz.why: Doesn't ya marca la tercera persona; el verbo queda en forma base.
quiz.why_en: Doesn't already carries the third person; the verb stays in base form.

quiz.q: Respuesta corta a «Do you live here?»
quiz.q_en: Short answer to "Do you live here?"
quiz.why: La respuesta corta repite el auxiliar: Yes, I do.
quiz.why_en: The short answer repeats the auxiliary: Yes, I do.

lecciones.content_es:
Para decir qué hay

There is + singular · There are + plural.

  • There is a board in the classroom.
  • There are 30 students.

Negativo y pregunta

  • There isn't a computer. / There aren't any maps.
  • Is there a library? → Yes, there is. / No, there isn't.
  • Are there any windows? → Yes, there are.

Truco

El verbo concuerda con lo que viene después: There is a pencil and two books (mira el primer elemento).
lecciones.content_en:
Saying what exists

There is + singular · There are + plural.

  • There is a board in the classroom.
  • There are 30 students.

Negative and question

  • There isn't a computer. / There aren't any maps.
  • Is there a library? → Yes, there is. / No, there isn't.
  • Are there any windows? → Yes, there are.

Tip

The verb agrees with what comes next: There is a pencil and two books.

fichas.d: Hay (singular): There is a chair.
fichas.d_en: Used with singular nouns: There is a chair.

fichas.d: Hay (plural): There are two chairs.
fichas.d_en: Used with plural nouns: There are two chairs.

fichas.d: Preguntas: se invierte there y el verbo.
fichas.d_en: Questions: there and the verb swap places.

fichas.d: Negación en plural, normalmente con any.
fichas.d_en: Plural negative, usually with any.

quiz.why: Four windows es plural, así que se usa There are.
quiz.why_en: Four windows is plural, so we use There are.

quiz.q: ¿Cómo se pregunta si hay una biblioteca?
quiz.q_en: How do you ask if there is a library?
quiz.why: En la pregunta el verbo is se pone antes de there.
quiz.why_en: In the question the verb is goes before there.

quiz.why: El verbo concuerda con el primer elemento de la lista: a teacher.
quiz.why_en: The verb agrees with the first item in the list: a teacher.

lecciones.content_es:
Preguntas de información

No se responden con sí o no: piden un dato.

  • What – qué · Who – quién · Where – dónde
  • When – cuándo · Why – por qué · How – cómo

El orden

Wh- + auxiliar + sujeto + verbo: Where do you live? · What does she study?

Con to be no hay auxiliar: Who is your teacher?

Demostrativos que suelen acompañarlas

this / that (singular), these / those (plural): What is this? What are those?
lecciones.content_en:
Information questions

They are not answered with yes or no: they ask for a piece of information.

  • What · Who · Where
  • When · Why · How

The order

Wh- + auxiliary + subject + verb: Where do you live? · What does she study?

With to be there is no auxiliary: Who is your teacher?

Demonstratives that go with them

this / that (singular), these / those (plural): What is this? What are those?

fichas.d: Qué, quién, dónde. Abren preguntas de información.
fichas.d_en: They open information questions.

fichas.d: Cuándo, por qué, cómo.
fichas.d_en: Time, reason and manner questions.

fichas.d: Orden fijo de la pregunta en presente simple.
fichas.d_en: Fixed word order for simple present questions.

fichas.d: Demostrativos: cerca/lejos, singular/plural.
fichas.d_en: Demonstratives: near/far, singular/plural.

quiz.q: «___ do you go to school?» — «By bus.»
quiz.q_en: "___ do you go to school?" — "By bus."
quiz.why: By bus responde al modo, y el modo se pregunta con How.
quiz.why_en: By bus answers manner, and manner is asked with How.

quiz.why: Wh- + auxiliar do + sujeto + verbo base.
quiz.why_en: Wh- + auxiliary do + subject + base verb.

quiz.why: Se pregunta por cosas, así que se usa What con el plural those.
quiz.why_en: We are asking about things, so we use What with the plural those.

lecciones.t: Saludos, fechas y comandos de clase
lecciones.content_es:
Saludos y despedidas

Formales: Good morning / Good afternoon / Good evening. Informales: Hi! Hello! What's up? Al despedirse: Goodbye, See you later, Have a nice day.

La fecha

Se dice con número ordinal: March 5th, 2026 → March the fifth. Días y meses van siempre en mayúscula: Monday, July.

Comandos de clase

  • Open your book / Close the door
  • Listen and repeat / Raise your hand
  • Work in pairs / Be quiet, please
lecciones.content_en:
Greetings and farewells

Formal: Good morning / Good afternoon / Good evening. Informal: Hi! Hello! What's up? Saying goodbye: Goodbye, See you later, Have a nice day.

The date

It uses an ordinal number: March 5th, 2026 → March the fifth. Days and months are always capitalized: Monday, July.

Classroom commands

  • Open your book / Close the door
  • Listen and repeat / Raise your hand
  • Work in pairs / Be quiet, please

fichas.d: Saludos formales según la hora del día.
fichas.d_en: Formal greetings depending on the time of day.

fichas.d: Despedida informal: nos vemos luego.
fichas.d_en: Informal farewell.

fichas.d: Días y meses siempre con mayúscula inicial en inglés.
fichas.d_en: Days and months are always capitalized in English.

fichas.d: Levanta la mano: comando típico de clase.
fichas.d_en: A typical classroom command.

fichas.d: La fecha usa número ordinal: the fifth.
fichas.d_en: The date uses an ordinal number: the fifth.

quiz.q: Son las 8 de la mañana. ¿Cómo saludas formalmente?
quiz.q_en: It is 8 a.m. How do you greet someone formally?
quiz.why: Good morning se usa desde el amanecer hasta el mediodía.
quiz.why_en: Good morning is used from sunrise until noon.

quiz.q: ¿Cuál fecha está bien escrita en inglés?
quiz.q_en: Which date is correctly written in English?
quiz.why: El mes va en mayúscula y el día en ordinal: March 5th.
quiz.why_en: The month is capitalized and the day is ordinal: March 5th.

quiz.why: Pair significa pareja: trabajar de a dos.
quiz.why_en: Pair means two people working together.

lecciones.content_es:
Materias

  • Math – matemáticas · Science – ciencias · Biology – biología
  • History – historia · Geography – geografía · Spanish – español
  • English – inglés · Art – artes · P.E. (Physical Education) – educación física
  • Music – música · Computer Science – informática

Cómo hablar de ellas

My favorite subject is Art. · I have English on Mondays and Wednesdays. · I'm good at Math.

Los nombres de las materias que son idiomas o países van con mayúscula: English, Spanish, French.
lecciones.content_en:
Subjects

  • Math · Science · Biology
  • History · Geography · Spanish
  • English · Art · P.E. (Physical Education)
  • Music · Computer Science

How to talk about them

My favorite subject is Art. · I have English on Mondays and Wednesdays. · I'm good at Math.

Subjects that are languages or countries are capitalized: English, Spanish, French.

fichas.d: Physical Education: educación física.
fichas.d_en: Physical Education.

fichas.d: Estructura para decir cuál es tu materia preferida.
fichas.d_en: Structure to say which subject you prefer.

fichas.d: Soy bueno en… Se usa con la materia: I'm good at Science.
fichas.d_en: Used with a subject: I'm good at Science.

fichas.d: Los lunes. Días en plural para hablar de rutina.
fichas.d_en: Plural days to talk about a routine.

quiz.why: P.E. es la sigla de Physical Education.
quiz.why_en: P.E. stands for Physical Education.

quiz.why: La expresión fija es to be good at something.
quiz.why_en: The fixed expression is to be good at something.

quiz.why: Los idiomas siempre llevan mayúscula inicial.
quiz.why_en: Languages are always capitalized.

lecciones.content_es:
Miembros de la familia

  • mother/mom – mamá · father/dad – papá · parents – padres
  • sister – hermana · brother – hermano · siblings – hermanos
  • grandmother – abuela · grandfather – abuelo
  • aunt – tía · uncle – tío · cousin – primo o prima
  • son – hijo · daughter – hija

Presentarlos

This is my sister. Her name is Laura. She is 15 years old.

Ojo: cousin sirve para primo y prima; parents son los padres, no los parientes (esos son relatives).
lecciones.content_en:
Family members

  • mother/mom · father/dad · parents
  • sister · brother · siblings
  • grandmother · grandfather
  • aunt · uncle · cousin
  • son · daughter

Introducing them

This is my sister. Her name is Laura. She is 15 years old.

Careful: cousin is used for both genders; parents means mother and father, while other family members are relatives.

fichas.d: Padres (mamá y papá). No significa parientes.
fichas.d_en: Mother and father, not relatives in general.

fichas.d: Hermanos y hermanas en conjunto.
fichas.d_en: Brothers and sisters together.

fichas.d: Primo o prima: la misma palabra para ambos.
fichas.d_en: The same word for male and female.

fichas.d: Fórmula para presentar a alguien.
fichas.d_en: Formula to introduce someone.

quiz.q: La hermana de mi mamá es mi…
quiz.why: Aunt es tía; cousin es primo o prima.
quiz.why_en: Aunt is the sister of a parent; cousin is the child of an aunt or uncle.

quiz.why: Siblings agrupa a hermanos y hermanas sin distinguir género.
quiz.why_en: Siblings covers brothers and sisters without marking gender.

quiz.q: «___ is my brother. ___ name is Juan.»
quiz.q_en: "___ is my brother. ___ name is Juan."
quiz.why: This presenta a una persona cercana y his es el posesivo masculino.
quiz.why_en: This introduces someone close and his is the masculine possessive.

lecciones.content_es:
Adjetivos

Describen al sustantivo y en inglés van antes de él: a tall boy, no a boy tall. Además nunca cambian: tall boys, no talls boys.

  • Apariencia: tall, short, thin, strong
  • Carácter: kind, funny, shy, smart
  • Cosas: big, small, new, old, expensive

Artículos

  • a antes de sonido consonante: a book
  • an antes de sonido vocal: an apple, an hour
  • the cuando ya se sabe de cuál hablamos: the teacher of my class
lecciones.content_en:
Adjectives

They describe the noun and in English they go before it: a tall boy, not a boy tall. They also never change: tall boys, not talls boys.

  • Appearance: tall, short, thin, strong
  • Character: kind, funny, shy, smart
  • Things: big, small, new, old, expensive

Articles

  • a before a consonant sound: a book
  • an before a vowel sound: an apple, an hour
  • the when we both know which one: the teacher of my class

fichas.d: a red car, no a car red.
fichas.d_en: a red car, not a car red.

fichas.d: No tienen plural: two big houses.
fichas.d_en: They have no plural form: two big houses.

fichas.d: an va antes de sonido vocálico: an apple, an hour.
fichas.d_en: an goes before a vowel sound: an apple, an hour.

fichas.d: Artículo definido: algo ya conocido o único.
fichas.d_en: Definite article: something known or unique.

quiz.why: El adjetivo va antes del sustantivo y en singular con a.
quiz.why_en: The adjective goes before the noun and stays singular after a.

quiz.why: Umbrella empieza con sonido vocálico, así que lleva an.
quiz.why_en: Umbrella starts with a vowel sound, so it takes an.

quiz.why: Kind (amable) describe la personalidad, no el aspecto físico.
quiz.why_en: Kind describes personality, not physical appearance.

repaso.titulo: Repaso — This Is Me: School Life and Daily Routines
repaso.titulo_en: Review — This Is Me: School Life and Daily Routines
repaso.resumen_es:
Lo esencial del periodo

Aprendiste a presentarte y a describir tu vida escolar. El motor del periodo es el presente simple: se usa para rutinas y verdades generales, agrega -s en he/she/it y necesita do/does para negar y preguntar.

Herramientas

  • To be para identidad, edad y estados: I am, you are, he is.
  • Pronombres (I, you, he…) y posesivos (my, your, his…): el sujeto nunca se omite.
  • There is / There are para decir qué hay en un lugar.
  • Wh- questions para pedir información: Wh- + auxiliar + sujeto + verbo.

Vocabulario

Saludos, fechas y comandos de clase; asignaturas; familia; adjetivos y artículos a/an/the.
repaso.resumen_en:
The core of the term

You learned to introduce yourself and describe your school life. The engine of the term is the simple present: it is used for routines and general truths, adds -s with he/she/it, and needs do/does for negatives and questions.

Tools

  • To be for identity, age and states: I am, you are, he is.
  • Pronouns (I, you, he…) and possessives (my, your, his…): the subject is never dropped.
  • There is / There are to say what a place contains.
  • Wh- questions to ask for information: Wh- + auxiliary + subject + verb.

Vocabulary

Greetings, dates and classroom commands; school subjects; family; adjectives and the articles a/an/the.
puntos_clave: La edad se dice con to be: I am 12 years old.
Age uses to be: I am 12 years old.
Solo he/she/it lleva -s en presente simple.
Only he/she/it takes -s in the simple present.
Con do/does el verbo principal vuelve a su forma base.
With do/does the main verb goes back to its base form.
There is + singular, There are + plural.
There is + singular, There are + plural.
El adjetivo va antes del sustantivo y no tiene plural.
The adjective goes before the noun and has no plural.

preguntas.why: My cousins es plural: le corresponde are.
preguntas.why_en: My cousins is plural: it takes are.
